`test_core_manager_restart_state_init_execution_path_lines_case` builds a dummy object whose `restart`, `dump_state`, and `_stop` methods are borrowed from `Qtile`, then calls `probe.restart()`. In `manager.py`, `restart` first checks `supports_restarting`, then calls `self.config.load()` inside the `try`; because the test expects one load call and no exception handling path, execution continues through the restart setup, opens the state file, and calls `self.dump_state(f)`. `dump_state` pickles `QtileState(self)`, so `QtileState.__init__` runs: it initializes attributes, iterates over three non-`ScratchPad` groups taking the `elif restart` branch each time, then iterates over two screens and updates `current_screen` when it reaches the current one.
